a2-dance: That's why I'd tell everyone not to dance on MDMA at all, however good the music is, since dancing makes the heat and the sweat that drain their salt. And really, what's the point of MDMA if someone wants to dance? For that they can take some San Pedro cactus or mescaline, which is way way safer, and still very therapeutic. Real MDMA, the kind that's therapeutic and helps people access very early childhood trauma, possibly better than San Pedro can in some cases, isn't the kind people want to dance on, which is why you don't see people in the MAPS trials of MDMA therapy saying "I NEED TO DANCE!" No, they're sitting there doing the therapy, and even if the science isn't clear on this yet, I and everyone I know are totally clear about what the real thing feels like. It's not like "I don't feel like dancing", it's like "I can barely move", couch lock. And in the same exact setting, the pills have gone both ways on me: some had me wanting to dance, and some left me in that couch lock. So if a pill makes someone feel like dancing, I'm highly suspicious that it contains amphetamines, or that it isn't real MDMA at all, maybe 6-APB, a similar drug. That might also be why women get low sodium far more often than men outside the lab, where what people take as "MDMA" is ecstasy, while a lab study that gave people pure MDMA and water found no difference between them. Then again, the lab dosed everyone by their weight, and at a festival a small woman takes the same pill as a big guy, so she's getting a lot more for her size.
a2-ss6: Overstimulating also dehydrates them, but we can't give fluids unless they're fully alert, able to swallow and not vomiting, and then just small sips of an electrolyte drink. If they still show the signs of low electrolytes from MDMA: Magnesium Alarm above, they may need more salt, potassium and magnesium than a normal electrolyte drink has. Salty potato chips give the salt and the potassium with nothing to cook, so I'd let them eat as many as they want. That's the only way I'd give potassium, since too much pure potassium is dangerous for anyone. Their potassium could be running high as well as low, though: MDMA can drain it, but muscles breaking down into the blood push it up. So if they start vomiting or get diarrhea, I'd stop the chips, since too much potassium brings those on and the chips have to stop either way while they're being sick. Magnesium also runs low in many people with serotonin syndrome (a nursing review). Magnesium chloride tastes too bad for most people to drink, but the skin absorbs it, so I'd stir a handful of magnesium chloride flakes into a little water and rub the mix on their skin. If you don't have the flakes, Epsom salt, which is magnesium sulfate rather than a kind of table salt, works the same way, just less well. If they can stand the taste, they can also take magnesium chloride by mouth, especially with MDMA-related jaw tension or twitching (the amounts are in MDMA: Magnesium Alarm, above).
a2-ss8: Since a seizure is one of the main dangers while you wait, I'd use DMSO, which seems to help prevent them, going by people's reports rather than studies: at any sign of an overdose, have them smell it or rub a little on a clean patch of skin (with 30% water if the skin itches), then use a little more at a time, since some people react more strongly than others. You might also think of niacin, which this guide uses for ending a trip, but it's unsafe with serotonin syndrome, since at that dose it can cause flushing and a drop in blood pressure (NIH). The other remedy I'd keep for a last resort, if nothing else is helping and no medics are coming, is Syrian rue oil, since it makes trips, ayahuasca included, much less intense. The oil isn't the Syrian rue brew from step 1, which blocks MAO and is dangerous with MDMA for that reason, but nobody has studied the oil with MDMA either.
